la:prep:cis.gloss: on or to this or the near side of; short of
senses: on or to this or the near side of; short of
la:prep:cis.html:
cis, prep.
pronom. stem ki-, whence -ce; Gr. ἐ-κεῖ; cf.: hic, sic, etc.
(far more rare than the kindr. citra),
on this side (opp. uls, ultra, and trans; cf. Müll.; ; ); with acc.
In space.
With verb of motion (rare): eo die cis Tiberim redeundum est, Varr. ap. .—
With verb of rest: Oppius mons, terticeps cis lucum Exquilinum, Sacr. Argae. ap. Müll.: cis Tiberim redire,: Gallia cis Rhenum perdomita, Dietsch; cf.: quae cis Taurum sunt,: cis Euphratem,: Germanos, qui cis Rhenum incolunt,: hic primus cis Anienem cum rege Veientium conflixit. : cis Taurum montem usque ad Halyn amnem,: cis Padum ultraque,; .—
In time, within (only in Plaut. and post-class. writers; in the former always in connection with pauci): cis dies paucos,: paucos cis mensīs, Lorenz ad loc.: cis paucas tempestates,: cis pauculos dies,: cis mensem decimum,.—
Acc. to Priscian, also in other designations of limits = intra: cis naturae leges, ut ultra naturae leges, P.; but the only passage cited for this meaning is: veniam petens, quod ei cis Vettios, Plautios dissimulavisset, Ritter (Halm: ei Titios, Vettios; al. aliter), a very corrupt passage.

la:noun:cista.gloss: a trunk, a chest, a casket
senses: a trunk, a chest, a casket
la:noun:cista.html:
cista, ae, f., = κίστη,
a wooden box or basket, often woven of slips or twigs, used for keeping money, clothes, books, fruit, etc.
In gen., ; ; ; * ; ; ; Poët. ap. ; ; ; .—
Esp.
In mystical religious festivals, a box for holding the sacred utensils, ; ; ; ; ; , p. 262.—
A box for depositing the votes in assemblies of the people, ; Sisenn. ap. ; ; Ascon. ap. ; cf. Dict. of Antiq.
